title: Barbara Kruger: Twelve

description.main: A 16-page book produced for Barbara Kruger's video installation Twelve at Tramway, Glasgow, in 2005, with extracts from a conversation between Kruger and John Calcutt.
description.extended:
This 16-page hardcover accompanied Barbara Kruger's video installation Twelve at Tramway, Glasgow, from 5 August to 26 September 2005.

Twelve, first shown at Mary Boone Gallery in New York in April 2004, is a video installation of twelve short scenes written by Kruger, performed by actors and projected on opposite sides of the room, with the viewer standing in the middle. Nine of the scenes take place around a meal, and the talk among friends and family turns more and more hostile. Text scrolling along the bottom of each scene suggests what the speakers think or say. The book includes extracts from a conversation between Kruger and John Calcutt.

The Tramway show partnered Kruger's first exhibition in Scotland, at Glasgow's Gallery of Modern Art. Both were part of Rule of Thumb, a 13-month programme on contemporary art, human rights and violence against women, developed by Glasgow City Council with Amnesty International UK and Rape Crisis Scotland.
description.artist_bio: Barbara Kruger (b. 1945, Newark) is an American artist who pairs found photographs with declarative text. She worked as a designer and picture editor at Conde Nast magazines, including Mademoiselle, before turning to photocollage in the late 1970s. She received the Golden Lion for lifetime achievement at the 51st Venice Biennale in 2005.
description.exhibition_context: Tramway showed Twelve as the partner to Kruger's first Scottish exhibition at the Gallery of Modern Art, Glasgow (21 April to 26 September 2005), within the Rule of Thumb programme.

notes: Produced to accompany the exhibition Twelve at Tramway, Glasgow, 5 August to 26 September 2005 (Library of Congress note). 16 pages, hardcover. Library of Congress and Open Library give the publisher as Tramway, Glasgow; some retail listings name Cornerhouse Publications. Dimensions not found. The available cover image is small (364 x 500 px).
